products.name: Daily Fluid
products.short: A fluid so light it disappears into the skin, with very high protection against UVB and UVA. The last step every morning, under make-up or on its own.
claims: UVA protection of at least a third of the SPF
products.use: Apply generously as the last step of your morning routine, 15 minutes before going out. Two full pumps cover face, neck and ears. Reapply every two hours outdoors, and after sweating or swimming.
details: Broad-spectrum filters: Tinosorb S, Tinosorb M, Uvinul A Plus, Uvinul T150

ingredients.name: Tinosorb S and Tinosorb M
ingredients.role: Photostable broad-spectrum filters covering UVB and the whole UVA range, including long UVA.

ingredients.name: Uvinul A Plus
ingredients.role: A dedicated UVA filter that keeps the UVA ratio above the EU minimum through the day.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide 4%
ingredients.role: Supports the barrier, evens tone and calms redness after sun exposure.

ingredients.name: Vitamin E
ingredients.role: An antioxidant that limits the free radicals the filters do not stop.

ingredients.name: Panthenol and glycerin

Notified in the EU Cosmetic Products Notification Portal before sale

faq.q: Can I wear it under foundation?
faq.a: Yes. Let it settle for a minute, then apply make-up as usual. It leaves no white cast and no greasy film.

faq.q: How much should I use?
faq.a: Two full pumps for face, neck and ears. SPF is tested at 2 mg per square centimetre; using half the amount gives far less than half the protection.

faq.q: Do I need to reapply if I work indoors?
faq.a: Indoors behind glass, one morning application is usually enough. Outdoors, reapply every two hours and after sweating or swimming.

faq.q: Which shade should I choose?
faq.a: Light suits fair to light skin, Medium suits light to olive skin, Deep suits tan to deep skin. The coverage is sheer, so a shade slightly off still blends. Two shades can be mixed.

faq.q: Does it replace foundation?
faq.a: For most days, yes. It evens out tone without covering freckles. For more coverage, use it as a base under your usual foundation.

faq.q: Why SPF 50 and not 50+?
faq.a: A pure zinc formula reaches SPF 50 reliably; pushing it to 50+ would mean more zinc and a heavier texture. SPF 50 blocks about 98 percent of UVB.

faq.q: Is it suitable during pregnancy?
faq.a: Zinc oxide is the filter most often recommended during pregnancy. The formula contains no fragrance, no retinoids and no chemical filters. Ask your midwife or doctor if you are unsure.

faq.q: Will it look white on deeper skin?
faq.a: The warm tint is designed to blend on most skin tones. On deep skin a faint sheen can remain; Tinted Fluid in Deep is the alternative.

faq.q: Why SPF 30 and not 50?
faq.a: A lip balm is reapplied many times a day, and SPF 30 already blocks about 97 percent of UVB. Higher filter loads make a balm waxy and bitter.

faq.q: Can it help against cold sores?
faq.a: UV exposure is a common trigger for cold sores. Daily SPF on the lips reduces that trigger; it does not treat an outbreak.

faq.q: It tingles slightly. Is that normal?
faq.a: A short warming or tingling on application is normal at pH 3.2. If it stings or stays red, use it every other morning for two weeks.

faq.q: Why 10 percent and not 20?
faq.a: Ten percent gives most of the benefit with far less irritation. With ferulic acid and vitamin E the photoprotection is already at its peak.

faq.q: What if it turns orange?
faq.a: A faint straw colour is normal. Deep orange means the vitamin C has oxidised; replace the bottle.
